Run the CTAS engine over a combined study input

Analyze_CTAS.Rd

A gsm-friendly wrapper around ctas::process_a_study(). It validates the input list produced by Combine_CTAS_Input(), applies reproducible seeding, and converts the degenerate cases CTAS signals by returning NULL elements into an informative error.

Usage

Analyze_CTAS(
  lInput,
  strFeatures = "autocorr;average;sd;unique_value_count_relative",
  nMinTimepoints = 3,
  nMinSubjects = 3,
  dMaxShareMissing = 0.5,
  bChangeFromBaseline = FALSE,
  bAutogenerate = TRUE,
  strScoringMethod = "ks",
  strPadjustMethod = "fdr",
  nSeed = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

lInput

list Result of Combine_CTAS_Input().

strFeatures

character Semicolon-delimited CTAS features.

nMinTimepoints

numeric Minimum timepoints per timeseries.

nMinSubjects

numeric Minimum subjects per timeseries.

dMaxShareMissing

numeric Maximum share of missing timepoints.

bChangeFromBaseline

logical Derive change-from-baseline timeseries.

bAutogenerate

logical Autogenerate timeseries.

strScoringMethod

character One of "ks", "mixedeffects", "avg_feat_value".

strPadjustMethod

character Passed to stats::p.adjust().

nSeed

numeric Optional seed for reproducibility.

...

Further arguments passed to ctas::process_a_study().

Value

list with timeseries, timeseries_features, PCA_coordinates and site_scores.

Details

process_a_study() is an all-metrics-at-once engine: a single call scores every (timeseries x feature x site) combination. It is therefore intended to run once per study, in a high-Priority mapping workflow, with each metric workflow filtering the shared result to one feature.

Examples

# \donttest{
lInput <- Combine_CTAS_Input(
  Input_Numeric(pharmaversesdtm::vs),
  dfSubjects = Input_Subjects(pharmaversesdtm::dm)
)
lCTAS <- Analyze_CTAS(lInput)
